findings.description: Three E-prime violations in body text: 'Self-determination is the precondition' (line 29), 'The first is political self-determination / The second is economic self-determination / The third is the floor clause' (line 37), 'This is not a new dynamic' and 'What differs is the scale and the pace' (line 45). Bare copula 'is' throughout body prose.
findings.suggestion: Line 29: 'Self-determination functions as the precondition, not merely one right among others.' Line 37: 'The first component covers political self-determination... The second covers economic self-determination... The third establishes the floor clause.' Line 45: 'This dynamic does not break new ground in labor economics... What changes involves scale and pace.'
findings.context: Self-determination is the precondition, not merely one right among others.

findings.description: E-prime violations in lensFraming frontmatter: politician lens uses 'self-determination is the precondition for all other rights'; researcher lens uses 'the right to self-determination is fundamental'; educator lens uses 'the question is not only whether a given individual can exercise economic rights'. Frontmatter prose should follow the same E-prime discipline as body content.
findings.suggestion: Politician lens: 'self-determination functions as the precondition for all other rights'. Researcher lens: 'the right to self-determination stands as fundamental' or 'the right to self-determination grounds all other rights'. Educator lens: 'the question asks not only whether a given individual can exercise economic rights'.
findings.context: Self-determination is the precondition for all other rights. [politician lens, line 21]

findings.description: E-prime violation in summary frontmatter: 'the right to economic self-determination is not merely aspirational'. The summary field renders in the site's meta description and social sharing previews — high-visibility location.
findings.suggestion: Rewrite: 'the right to economic self-determination reaches beyond aspiration — it names the exact terrain at stake.'
findings.context: the right to economic self-determination is not merely aspirational — it describes the exact terrain at stake.

findings.description: 'automation has always shifted returns toward capital' stated as unqualified historical fact. Long-run economic history challenges this: the industrial revolution eventually produced substantial real-wage increases across working populations. The claim holds in the short run and for certain automation waves but does not hold universally across time horizons and automation types.
findings.suggestion: Hedge to scope: 'automation typically concentrates initial productivity gains in capital before competitive and redistributive pressures widen returns' or 'automation historically shifts short-run returns toward capital, with longer-run distributional outcomes varying by policy context'.
findings.context: This is not a new dynamic in labor economics; automation has always shifted returns toward capital.

findings.description: Summary frontmatter presents an interpretive conclusion as definitional: 'it describes the exact terrain at stake'. The connection between ICESCR Article 1 and AI labor displacement constitutes an interpretive extension (correctly flagged at body line 80) — presenting it as axiomatic in the high-visibility summary field without qualification front-loads the advocacy over the analysis.
findings.suggestion: Rewrite to flag the interpretive nature: 'the right to economic self-determination names the structural terrain that AI-driven labor displacement enters — a terrain the United States has chosen to leave unaccountable.'
findings.context: it describes the exact terrain at stake.

findings.description: Voter lens: 'A society's ability to collectively shape how a transformative technology distributes its benefits is precisely what Article 1 protects.' The phrase 'is precisely what Article 1 protects' presents a broad interpretive extension as definitional. Article 1 drafted for decolonization; its application to technology distribution constitutes interpretive argument, not settled doctrine. Also contains E-prime violation ('is precisely what').
findings.suggestion: Rewrite: 'A society's ability to collectively shape how a transformative technology distributes its benefits falls within the scope of what Article 1 was written to protect — though that application to AI remains contested in international law.' This preserves the advocacy while marking the interpretive nature.
findings.context: A society's ability to collectively shape how a transformative technology distributes its benefits is precisely what Article 1 protects.

findings.description: Body text: 'the structural pattern Article 1 addresses recurs in a new form' — the article's central analogy (data-as-natural-resources, AI displacement as structural dispossession) stated as observation rather than as the interpretive argument it represents. The epistemic flag at line 80 correctly identifies this as 'an interpretive extension' with no CESCR General Comment support, but the flag appears after the body prose, reducing its salience for readers who encounter the claim first.
findings.suggestion: Add an inline hedge at the point of claim: 'the structural pattern Article 1 addresses appears to recur in a new form — though no CESCR General Comment has yet applied the doctrine to digital resources.' This moves the qualification to the claim site rather than deferring it to the epilogue.
findings.context: the structural pattern Article 1 addresses recurs in a new form.

payload.scan_notes: Single new article scanned (article-1-self-determination, published 2026-04-22). Article shows strong epistemic hygiene in its dedicated EPISTEMIC FLAGS section and correctly flags the Article 1 / AI intersection as 'nascent scholarship' and 'interpretive extension'. Main quality gaps: E-prime discipline in body and frontmatter prose (3 findings, lines 3/21/29/37/45), and fair-witness gap between the body's careful hedging and the summary/voter-lens framing which presents interpretive claims as definitional. Vocabulary dimension clean — ICESCR, ICCPR, CESCR all match glossary canonical forms. No structural issues detected (heading hierarchy consistent h2, no broken link patterns, no missing alt text).

epistemic_flags: E-prime detection relies on pattern matching — idiomatic or legal uses of 'to be' (e.g., 'not to be deprived') in quoted treaty language may represent false positives; findings f1-f3 target clear copula uses in original prose, not quoted text

Fair-witness assessment of the Article 1 / AI analogy (f5-f7) requires interpreting interpretive legal scholarship — the line between advocacy framing and overclaim involves judgment about register and audience expectation

Historical economics claim (f4) assessed against labor economics literature in training data; specific counterexamples (industrial revolution real wage trajectory) represent the mainstream economic history view but the literature contains heterodox positions
